No evidence of CNS stimulation has been reported in man al- though patients given atracurium12 had a 20% higher mean arte- rial-thiopental concentration at awakening compared with pa- tients given vecuronium, suggesting that laudanosine may have had a minor stimulatory effect on the CNS. The blood-brain bar- rier appears to be effective in preventing a very high concentra- tion of laudanosine from reaching the CNS and it is considered unlikely13 that concentrations great enough to provoke seizures will be reached.
